principles: Single choke-point beats whack-a-mole per-call-site fixes
Grep-contract is cheap and catches the defect class at the SOURCE, not just the symptoms
Preserve existing helper shapes (lab.ts/cli-engine.ts/declared-artifact-commit-check.ts runGit-style) — they have real stdout/exit-code value
Keep the two prior wrapper-root smokes byte-identical so we don't lose their existing assertions
drivers: A defect class has recurred across 5+ stories; per-call-site fixes do not prevent recurrence
Wrapper-root layout is the canonical OSS deployment topology — calls failing here block real operators
Contract tests are the team's established pattern, not eslint

options.name: Choke-point + grep contract (chosen)
cons: Grep contract has FP risk for edge syntax — needs careful regex + allowlist

options.name: ESLint custom rule
cons: High integration cost; team prefers smoke-test contracts

options.name: Per-call-site reroute only, no contract
cons: Does not prevent recurrence — same as the current state we're trying to escape

rationale: Aligns with team's existing smoke-test contract pattern (gitroot-cwd-routing-smoke, bare-gate-gitroot-cwd-smoke already exist); cheapest preventive measure; catches the defect AT THE SOURCE not just at the symptom.

preMortem.scenario: The grep contract has a regex false positive and starts failing on legitimate code
preMortem.trigger: Regex matches a STRING that contains 'execFileSync' / 'spawnSync' inside a comment or another smoke-fixture file
preMortem.consequence: CI breaks for unrelated changes; team disables the contract
preMortem.mitigation: Scope the grep to actual call-expression syntax (e.g. match `(execFileSync|spawnSync|execSync)\(['\"']git['\"']`); exclude test/smoke files and existing fixture files via an explicit allowlist; add a self-test where the contract smoke runs against a small fixture of known-good + known-bad samples

preMortem.scenario: Rerouting a call site changes runtime behavior because the caller relied on cwd defaulting to process.cwd() (not metadataRoot)
preMortem.trigger: Some sites pass `{cwd}` implicitly assuming process.cwd; rerouting forces an explicit resolved cwd
preMortem.consequence: Subtle regressions where git ran in a different dir than before
preMortem.mitigation: For each site, READ the caller context before rewriting; for sites that genuinely want process.cwd, leave them untouched and document via allowlist; the 2 existing smokes (gitroot-cwd-routing, bare-gate-gitroot-cwd) must still pass byte-identically — they are the strongest existing safety net

preMortem.scenario: resolveGitCwd is itself a git child-process caller (via internal probes) and the grep contract flags it as a bare-projectRoot site
preMortem.trigger: resolveGitCwd internally calls git rev-parse to verify the gitRoot — chicken-and-egg
preMortem.consequence: Contract smoke fails on the helper itself
preMortem.mitigation: Allowlist resolveGitCwd's own file (story-signed-workspace-resolution.ts) and the 3 ad-hoc helpers in the contract smoke's allowlist; the allowlist is part of the contract source, reviewable in the same PR

preMortem.scenario: The 193 number undercounts (e.g. helpers like runGit hide additional git calls inside them, or template strings produce `git` as a variable)
preMortem.consequence: Some call sites are missed in the audit, defect class is not fully killed
preMortem.mitigation: Cross-check with `git grep -nE "['\"']git['\"'],\s*\[" -- 'packages/**/*.ts'` AND `git grep -nE "runGit\(|runGitNoThrow\(" -- 'packages/**/*.ts'`; the audit count must reconcile across both scans; the contract smoke covers the literal-git case, the wrapper helpers are themselves allowlisted but their callers go through the same audit
